definitions.explanation: A small olive-brown bird native to Japan, famous for its distinctive call ホーホケキョ. Associated with spring and considered one of Japan's most beloved birds.

examples.japanese: {鶯|うぐいす}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}いている→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{鶯|うぐいす}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえて→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧くる。
examples.english: When spring comes, you can hear the voice of the bush warbler.

examples.japanese: ⟦{早朝|そうちょう}→早朝：03109_souchou⟧、⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{止|と}まった→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧{鶯|うぐいす}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ホーホケキョ→ホーホケキョ：29102_hoohokekyo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{鳴|な}き→鳴く：04388_naku⟧、⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れ→訪れ：14267_otozure⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げた→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧。
examples.english: Early in the morning, a bush warbler perched on the plum tree in the garden and called "hōhokekyo," announcing the arrival of spring.

notes:
The uguisu is considered a herald of spring in Japanese culture. Its call ⟦ホーホケキョ→ホーホケキョ：29102_hoohokekyo⟧ is one of the most recognized bird sounds in Japan.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- {鶯|うぐいす}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{春告鳥|はるつげどり} (spring-heralding bird) as a poetic name
- ⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{鶯|うぐいす} (⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{鶯|うぐいす}): plum blossom and bush warbler — a classic pairing in Japanese art and poetry symbolizing early spring
- {鶯|うぐいす}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{初音|はつね}: the first call of the bush warbler in the new year — a classic seasonal theme

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {鶯|うぐいす}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧: the bush warbler sings
- {鶯|うぐいす}⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧: bush warbler color (yellow-green)
